A variable is a named place for a current value. Input supplies a value, processing changes or combines values, and output reports a result. Read instructions from top to bottom. An assignment replaces the old value; it does not keep every earlier value."},{"id":"example","kind":"EXAMPLE","title":"Worked example","body":"Start with count = 2. First run count = count + 3, so count becomes 5. Then run count = count * 2, so count becomes 10. Displaying count outputs 10. Reversing the two assignments would produce 7, so their order matters."},{"id":"guided","kind":"CHECK","title":"Guided check","body":"Apply the explanation, then inspect the corrective feedback.","questionId":"guided"},{"id":"bridge","kind":"READING","title":"Explain the rule","body":"Before continuing, separate the current value from the instruction. If count is 4, the instruction count = count + 2 replaces it with 6. Only the next instruction sees that updated 6. Writing the value after every line prevents using the original input twice."},{"id":"ordering","kind":"CHECK","title":"Trace the order","body":"Arrange the steps using the labeled movement controls.","questionId":"ordering"},{"id":"independent","kind":"CHECK","title":"Independent application","body":"Use the rule in this new small example.","questionId":"independent"},{"id":"summary","kind":"READING","title":"Summary and later review","body":"To trace a sequence independently, record each new value in order, then report the last value at the output instruction. Practice results here are demonstration study data, not a course grade."}]}],"questions":[{"id":"guided","format":"selected_response","prompt":"Which instruction is processing rather than input or output?","options":[{"id":"compute","text":"total = price * quantity","feedback":"This combines two values to compute a new value."},{"id":"read","text":"Read quantity from the keyboard","feedback":"Reading supplies input; it does not perform the multiplication."},{"id":"display","text":"Display total","feedback":"Displaying reports the result after processing."}],"answer":["compute"],"hint":"Look for the instruction that calculates a new value.","explanation":"Multiplication transforms the supplied values. v1.textJson: {"schemaVersion":1,"moduleId":"mock_data_structures","version":1,"lessons":[{"id":"lesson_1","title":"MOCK - Choosing a Stack or Queue","steps":[{"id":"goal","kind":"READING","title":"Goal and explanation","body":"MOCK ORIGINAL LESSON. A stack removes the most recently added item first: last in, first out (LIFO). A queue removes the earliest waiting item first: first in, first out (FIFO). The same stored items can therefore leave in different orders."},{"id":"example","kind":"EXAMPLE","title":"Worked example","body":"Add A, then B, then C. In a stack, the next removal returns C because it was added last. In a queue, the next removal returns A because it has waited longest. Both structures then contain two items; their removal rule, rather than their item count, distinguishes them."},{"id":"guided","kind":"CHECK","title":"Guided check","body":"Apply the explanation, then inspect the corrective feedback.","questionId":"guided"},{"id":"bridge","kind":"READING","title":"Explain the rule","body":"Keep order and count separate. Enqueue adds one item at the back; dequeue removes one item from the front. After four additions and two valid removals from a previously empty queue, two items remain. A removal from an empty structure is outside this example and must be handled explicitly in real software."},{"id":"ordering","kind":"CHECK","title":"Trace the order","body":"Arrange the steps using the labeled movement controls.","questionId":"ordering"},{"id":"independent","kind":"CHECK","title":"Independent application","body":"Use the rule in this new small example.","questionId":"independent"},{"id":"summary","kind":"READING","title":"Summary and later review","body":"Choose the structure from the required removal rule, then trace its operations. Stack means latest first; queue means earliest first. State empty-structure behavior separately rather than guessing."}]}],"questions":[{"id":"guided","format":"selected_response","prompt":"An undo history should return the most recent action first. Which structure matches that rule?","options":[{"id":"stack","text":"Stack","feedback":"The latest action is the last item added, matching LIFO."},{"id":"queue","text":"Queue","feedback":"FIFO would return the earliest action, rather than the latest one."}],"answer":["stack"],"hint":"Undo the last action before earlier actions.","explanation":"A stack returns the latest stored action first. This is a rule-selection example, not a full undo implementation."},{"id":"ordering","format":"ordering","prompt":"Order the next three removals from a queue that received A, then B, then C.","options":[{"id":"a","text":"Remove A","feedback":"A entered first, so FIFO removes it first."},{"id":"b","text":"Remove B","feedback":"B entered after A and before C."},{"id":"c","text":"Remove C","feedback":"C entered last and waits until the earlier items leave."}],"answer":["a","b","c"],"hint":"Follow the arrival order.","explanation":"FIFO preserves the arrival order for these removals: A, B, C."},{"id":"independent","format":"bounded_response","prompt":"An empty queue receives four items, then performs two valid removals. How many items remain?","responseType":"numeric","unit":"items","target":2,"tolerance":0,"hint":"Each addition increases the count by one; each removal decreases it by one.","explanation":"Four additions produce four items. Two removals leave 4 - 2 = 2 items."},{"id":"review_1","format":"bounded_response","prompt":"Name the structure that removes the most recently added item first.","responseType":"short","unit":"","acceptedAnswers":["stack"],"caseSensitive":false,"hint":"Its removal rule is LIFO.","explanation":"A stack follows last in, first out."},{"id":"review_2","format":"bounded_response","prompt":"A queue receives D, E and F, then removes D. How many items remain?","responseType":"numeric","unit":"items","target":2,"tolerance":0,"hint":"One item leaves the three-item queue.","explanation":"E and F remain, so the count is two."}],"glossary":[{"term":"Stack","definition":"A structure whose next removal returns the most recently added remaining item."},{"term":"Queue","definition":"A structure whose next removal returns the earliest added remaining item."},{"term":"FIFO","definition":"First in, first out: the earliest waiting item leaves first."},{"term":"LIFO","definition":"Last in, first out: the most recently added item leaves first."}]}

A table organizes records as rows and attributes as columns. A primary key distinguishes each row and must be unique and present. Filtering selects matching rows; it does not rewrite the original table."},{"id":"example","kind":"EXAMPLE","title":"Worked example","body":"Consider rows (id=1, subject=computing), (id=2, subject=math), (id=3, subject=computing), (id=4, subject=art).
